{"filepath":"raw_findings.md","content":"# Raw findings: Commercial status of solid-state batteries (research notes)

Date compiled: 2026-09-06

Sources used (search limited):
- QuantumScape press releases and site: https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production
  (also https://www.quantumscape.com/category/press-releases/page/2 and https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-announces-shipment-of-b1-samples-achieving-a-key-annual-goal)
  - Credibility note: primary source (company press releases). Useful for announced milestones and company claims; may be forward-looking.

- Solid Power PR / coverage and SEC filing excerpts:
  - PR: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html
  - SEC filing mention: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm
  - Credibility note: PR and SEC filings are high-credibility for corporate announcements; PR is promotional, SEC 10-K/10-Q are legally required disclosures.

- ProLogium press release and coverage (notable TV test claims and production milestones):
  - ProLogium press release: https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies
  - PR Newswire coverage of Solid-State Summit claims: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prologium-technology-presented-its-film-free-next-generation-battery-technology-at-the-2024-solid-state-battery-summit-302255281.html
  - Third-party coverage of 381 Wh/kg mass-production claim (2026): https://interestingengineering.com/energy/prologium-solid-state-battery-mass-production-381-wh-kg
  - Credibility note: company PRs are primary but promotional. TV claims cited in PRs should be treated as third-party validation if the TV report is available; secondary media may summarize.

- CATL / China reports and media coverage (consortium, prototype claims, pilot timelines):
  - Electrek / broader coverage referencing CATL: https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030
  - Electrive / reporting: https://www.electrive.com/2026/03/13/catl-makes-progress-on-its-solid-state-battery
  - Credibility note: media coverage from Electrek/Electrive is secondary; useful for timelines and industry context but should be corroborated with CATL press releases (not retrieved in this search run).

Limitations: The web-search tool was available with a small search quota for this task and returned a subset of the ecosystem documents. The file below emphasizes findings from the retrieved documents (QuantumScape, Solid Power, ProLogium, and press/media about CATL). Additional authoritative sources (e.g., Toyota press releases on SSB, Samsung SDI announcements, BNEF/ICCT/UBS/Goldman research notes, peer-reviewed papers) were not fetched due to the search limit. Recommend a follow-up search round to fill gaps (Toyota official SSB program pages, Samsung/Panasonic press, analyst reports from BNEF/UBS/Goldman, regulatory filings from other firms, third-party test reports from TV, Intertek, or Fraunhofer).


---

Executive summary

- As of the sources retrieved (company press releases and media coverage through 2026), several companies have moved beyond laboratory R&D into pilot production, prototype shipments, or limited series production for variants of solid-state or "lithium ceramic" batteries. Notable named actors in these materials: QuantumScape (ceramic separator/solid-state Li-metal cells), Solid Power (sulfide solid electrolyte, pilot lines and partnerships), ProLogium (lithium-ceramic "film-free" cells and GWh-level factory in Taiwan), and large incumbents in China (CATL) pursuing solid / semi-solid approaches.
  - QuantumScape: inaugurated an automated pilot ("Eagle Line") and reported shipment of prototype/sample cells (B1/B1 shipments) as milestones in 2023–2024. Source: QuantumScape press releases. (https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production, https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-announces-shipment-of-b1-samples-achieving-a-key-annual-goal)
  - Solid Power: public announcements of pilot-line transitions and partnerships for pilot manufacturing; SEC filings note pilot line installations and continuous electrolyte line commissioning targeted (e.g., continuous electrolyte production by end of 2026 in filing). Source: Solid Power PR and SEC filing. (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm)
  - ProLogium: announced GWh-level Taoyuan/Taoke factory production in 2024 with certifications by TV reported for energy density claims (321 Wh/kg gravimetric; 749 Wh/L volumetric) and later mass-production claims (381 Wh/kg reported in 2026 coverage). Source: ProLogium PR and PR Newswire, and third-party coverage. (https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prologium-technology-presented-its-film-free-next-generation-battery-technology-at-the-2024-solid-state-battery-summit-302255281.html, https://interestingengineering.com/energy/prologium-solid-state-battery-mass-production-381-wh-kg)
  - CATL and Chinese consortia: media reports indicate semi-solid (hybrid) variants are already in low-volume series production in China (examples: WeLion/Nio partnership) while CATL targets small-scale all-solid-state production by around 2027 and broader commercialization later. Source: Electrek and Electrive coverage. (https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030, https://www.electrive.com/2026/03/13/catl-makes-progress-on-its-solid-state-battery)

- Across announcements, firm timelines vary and are frequently forward-looking. Company press releases and SEC filings indicate pilot lines and prototype shipments (2023–2026), with some companies (ProLogium, Chinese firms) claiming pilot or series production. Independent, third-party validation (e.g., regulatory test reports, peer-reviewed long-term cycle data) is relatively sparse in the retrieved set; many company claims are framed as milestones toward automotive qualification rather than full OEM-scale mass production.

- The main technical blockers cited across the literature and company disclosures are consistent: interface stability between Li-metal and solid electrolyte, dendrite penetration, stack pressure requirements, electrolyte manufacturability at scale (materials and roll-to-roll coating), yield and reproducibility, and supply-chain issues (materials for solid electrolytes, licensing/scale of ceramic coating equipment). See detailed blocker list below.


Companies actively commercializing or piloting (with announced product/stage and dates)

- QuantumScape (U.S.)
  - Announced: inauguration of the "Eagle Line" automated pilot production line (inauguration event press release, 2023–2024). Reported shipment of B1 prototype samples (goal reported for 2024).
  - Sources: https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production
    - Credibility: company primary source; reliable for public milestones but optimistic on timelines.

- Solid Power (U.S.)
  - Announced: transitioning silicon cells to a pilot line and platform technology updates; SEC filing notes pilot cell manufacturing line installation at SK On and continuous electrolyte production line commissioning expected by end of 2026.
  - Sources: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm
    - Credibility: PR and SEC filing; SEC filing especially credible for contractual/installation milestones.

- ProLogium (Taiwan) / "Lithium Ceramic Battery" (LCB)
  - Announced: GWh-level Gigafactory (Taoke) began production in 2024 per company release; PRs cite TÜV certifications (321 Wh/kg, 749 Wh/L) and rapid charge claims presented at 2024 Solid-State Battery Summit. Later media coverage (2026) reports mass production and a 381 Wh/kg 185.4 Ah cell (TÜV cited) — note date beyond 2024.
  - Sources: https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prologium-technology-presented-its-film-free-next-generation-battery-technology-at-the-2024-solid-state-battery-summit-302255281.html ; https://interestingengineering.com/energy/prologium-solid-state-battery-mass-production-381-wh-kg
    - Credibility: company PRs and PR Newswire (primary). Third-party media summarizes claims; TÜV mention increases credibility if the TÜV report is available for verification.

- CATL (China) and Chinese consortium partners
  - Announced/Reported: CATL is working on all-solid-state and semi-solid variants; Chinese semi-solid packs were reported in small series production and fielded by Chinese OEMs (examples noted in media: WeLion/Nio and SAIC MG4 semi-solid usage). Reports suggest CATL aims for small-scale all-solid-state production by ~2027 and further scale-up thereafter.
  - Sources: https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030 ; https://www.electrive.com/2026/03/13/catl-makes-progress-on-its-solid-state-battery
    - Credibility: media reports; need to corroborate with CATL primary press statements. Chinese firms tend to announce initiatives via state/industry consortiums and company PRs.

- Other firms frequently named in the ecosystem (not fully searched in this run but commonly reported in industry literature): Toyota, Samsung SDI, Panasonic, Ilika, Factorial Energy, WeLion / Enovix (semi-solid variants), and several startups in Japan/Europe. Specific current-status citations for these were not retrieved in this search due to quota.


Announced pilot lines / production capacities (selected)

- QuantumScape: "Eagle Line" — automated pilot production line installed at QuantumScape HQ (inaugurated 2023–2024; used for prototype/sample shipments). Source: https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production
  - Credibility: company press release.

- Solid Power: pilot cell manufacturing line installation at SK On facility (mentioned in SEC filing) and plans for commissioning continuous electrolyte production line by end of 2026. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html
  - Credibility: SEC filing is high credibility for contractual milestones.

- ProLogium: GWh-level gigafactory (Taoke) in Taoyuan, Taiwan reportedly began production in 2024; company reports >2.4 million battery units shipped as milestone. Source: https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies
  - Credibility: company press release; claims of shipments and factory operation are primary but should be cross-checked with independent production verification (e.g., TÜV test reports, third-party audit).

- CATL / Chinese semi-solid production: multiple China OEMs reportedly fielded semi-solid packs in limited series production (media reports reference Nio/WeLion and SAIC MG4 milestones). Source: Electrek reporting. (https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030)
  - Credibility: secondary media; needs corroboration with OEM and supplier announcements.


Reported cell performance metrics (energy density, cycle life, safety incidents, operating temperature)

- ProLogium (as reported in company PRs and coverage):
  - Reported metrics (per ProLogium / PR): 321 Wh/kg gravimetric and 749 Wh/L volumetric (TV certifications referenced in PRs for 2024 claims); later reported 381 Wh/kg for a 185.4 Ah cell in 2026 coverage (TV cited) when moving toward mass production.
  - Sources: https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prologium-technology-presented-its-film-free-next-generation-battery-technology-at-the-2024-solid-state-battery-summit-302255281.html ; https://interestingengineering.com/energy/prologium-solid-state-battery-mass-production-381-wh-kg
  - Credibility: company PR and PR Newswire; TÜV mention implies third-party testing, which increases credibility if the TÜV report is accessible.

- QuantumScape (company claims, general goals):
  - QuantumScape markets its cells as next-generation Li-metal solid-state cells aiming for higher energy density, faster charging, and enhanced safety. Specific energy-density/cycle-life numbers in the retrieved press releases emphasize milestones (Eagle Line, B1 sample shipments) but do not present a definitive long-term cycle-life number in these specific press releases. QuantumScape has historically published lab data in prior years (not re-fetched in this run).
  - Sources: https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production ; https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-announces-shipment-of-b1-samples-achieving-a-key-annual-goal
  - Credibility: company primary source; technical claims should be cross-checked with white papers, SEC filings, and independent testing.

- Solid Power (company statements and SEC filings):
  - Solid Power describes a sulfide solid-electrolyte approach and has discussed improving energy density and safety. SEC filings mention pilot lines and technology platform moves. Specific cycle-life/energy density numbers were not present in the retrieved headlines but are reported in other public materials historically (not fetched here).
  - Sources: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm
  - Credibility: SEC filing high; PR is primary.

- CATL and Chinese semi-solid packs:
  - Reported gains in energy density for prototype/all-solid designs (media summaries cite up to +40% in prototypes). Semi-solid packs in Chinese production lines are variations that mix solid-like components with liquid/gels and thus have different metrics. The retrieved media pieces did not include third-party validated cycle-life numbers or safety incident reports.
  - Sources: https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030 ; https://www.electrive.com/2026/03/13/catl-makes-progress-on-its-solid-state-battery
  - Credibility: secondary media; prototype numbers require independent verification.

- Safety incidents: none of the retrieved company press releases highlight safety incidents; companies present SSBs as safer alternatives to flammable liquid electrolytes. However, long-term reliability, thermal runaway pathways with solid electrolytes, and interface failures remain concerns in the literature.
  - Credibility: absence of incident reports in these press releases does not imply absence in testing — independent testing reports and OEM qualification data would be necessary to confirm safety in automotive contexts.


Announced manufacturing methods and materials (sulfide, oxide, polymer, composite) and scale-up demonstrations

- QuantumScape: ceramic/separator-focused solid-state lithium-metal cell approach (company describes ceramic thin-film separator / solid electrolyte stacks). The Eagle Line is an attempt to demonstrate automated manufacturing for their ceramic film and cell assembly.
  - Source: https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production
  - Credibility: company primary

- Solid Power: sulfide solid electrolyte platform (company materials and platform announcements). SEC filings reference pilot line installations and production transitions.
  - Source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html ; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm
  - Credibility: company primary and SEC

- ProLogium: brands its technology as "lithium ceramic battery (LCB)" with film-free manufacturing and ceramic-based electrolyte/architecture. Company PRs emphasize film-free (no polymer separator film) stacks and large-format cell production.
  - Source: https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/prologium-technology-presented-its-film-free-next-generation-battery-technology-at-the-2024-solid-state-battery-summit-302255281.html
  - Credibility: company primary

- CATL and Chinese consortia: working on both semi-solid and all-solid variants; manufacturing demonstrations for semi-solid packs were already pushed into production at limited scale by Chinese OEMs (WeLion/Nio, SAIC). CATL has patents and prototype demonstrations for various solid electrolyte chemistries (public details need further fetch).
  - Source: https://electrek.co/2026/06/25/catl-solid-state-battery-level-4-2030
  - Credibility: media coverage; corroboration with CATL primary statements recommended.

Scale-up demonstrations: retrieved documents show pilot lines, GWh-level factory claims (ProLogium), and pilot installations (QuantumScape Eagle Line, Solid Power pilot facilities). Independent verification (third-party plant visits, audited production figures) was not retrieved here.


Cost or cost-projection figures where available

- In the retrieved set there were no authoritative, detailed per-kWh cost figures from company press releases. Companies commonly claim improved cost trajectories through higher energy density (less pack-level cost per kWh) and manufacturing improvements but do not provide granular cost-per-kWh production numbers in these particular PRs.
  - Sources: (general references above).
  - Credibility: N/A — follow-up needed to fetch analyst reports or SEC statements that quantify COGS or forecast cost per kWh.


Notable patents or IP disputes reported

- The retrieved search results in this session did not return firm-specific patent litigation documents (e.g., QuantumScape patent disputes) within the limited query budget. Historically, IP is an active area (companies file extensive patents on solid electrolyte compositions, ceramic separator production, stack architecture, and manufacturing methods). Recommendation: targeted search for "QuantumScape patent lawsuit", "Solid Power patents", "ProLogium patents", and relevant patent office records (USPTO, EPO, CNIPA) for confirmation.
  - Credibility: patent filings are public and authoritative; disputes are often reported by trade press and legal filings.


Analyst timeline projections (summary of retrieved media/industry commentary)

- Media coverage and industry commentary in retrieved results indicate staggered timelines: pilot production and prototype shipments 2023–2026; small-scale/limited series production for semi-solid packs in China around 2023–2024; small-scale all-solid-state pilot goals in the mid-2020s (2026–2028) for some firms (CATL, Solid Power, QuantumScape), with broader OEM-scale commercialization often pushed toward the late 2020s or early 2030s in many analyst projections. Specific BNEF/UBS/Galliard timelines were not retrieved due to search limits.
  - Sources: electrek, Electrive, company PRs above.
  - Credibility: media/analyst summaries are useful for ranges but require referencing original analyst reports for precise probabilities and forecast methodology.


Explicit list of reported technical and supply-chain blockers (with short notes and citations)

- Interface stability (Li metal / solid electrolyte contact, interfacial resistance growth): repeatedly cited in the literature as a major technical challenge because solid-solid contact can develop gaps, increased resistance, or chemical reactions that degrade cycling. Company PRs often highlight interface engineering as a core R&D focus (QuantumScape, Solid Power). Source: QuantumScape press releases; Solid Power PR and SEC filing. (https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production ; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/solid-power-unveils-all-solid-state-platform-technology-transitions-silicon-cells-to-pilot-line-301297438.html)
  - Credibility: primary company statements; corroborate with academic literature for mechanistic detail.

- Dendrite formation / lithium penetration through solid electrolytes: Even with solid electrolytes, lithium metal can form filaments that penetrate the electrolyte or exploit defects. This continues to be an area of active research (cited generally in company materials and media). Source: company PRs and industry commentary (above).
  - Credibility: widespread academic and industry recognition; engineering mitigations remain under development.

- Stack pressure and mechanical requirements: Some solid-state designs require stack pressure or specialized cell compression hardware to maintain contact, which complicates pack-level integration and increases system complexity. Company pilot lines often test mechanical stacks for automotive qualification. Source: QuantumScape and ProLogium product architecture discussion in PRs.
  - Credibility: company PRs and independent analyses reported in trade media; recognized in technical literature.

- Electrolyte manufacturing scale-up (coating, ceramic film production, continuous processes): Scaling thin ceramic films or sulfide powders to roll-to-roll high-yield manufacturing without defects is frequently cited as a bottleneck. QuantumScape's Eagle Line and partner announcements (e.g., Murata collaboration historically) aim to address automated ceramic film production. Source: QuantumScape Eagle Line press release. (https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-inaugurates-eagle-line-for-solid-state-battery-pilot-production)
  - Credibility: company primary; manufacturing scale-up is a commonly noted industry barrier.

- Material supply and cost for solid electrolyte precursors and ceramic/separator materials: Availability and cost of specialized materials (e.g., sulfide powders, oxide precursors, ceramic thin-film materials) and specialized equipment (vacuum deposition, high-temperature sintering) can restrict rapid scale-up. Source: SEC filing remarks and industry analyses referenced in company PRs (Solid Power SEC filing mentions production line installation partners). (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1844862/000110465926019435/sldp-20251231x10k.htm)
  - Credibility: SEC filing and industry reports; supply chain constraints are widely reported across battery industry literature.

- Yield and reproducibility at scale (defect control): Achieving high yields for thin ceramic films and defect-free cell stacks is challenging; defects can lead to short circuits and low yields. Company pilot lines are explicitly targeted at learning to improve yield before scaling. Source: QuantumScape Eagle Line release, Solid Power pilot statements.
  - Credibility: company primary statements and manufacturing logic.

- Qualification & testing time (OEM automotive qualification): Automotive qualification requires long-term calendar and cycle testing, safety validation, and field reliability — a time-consuming and expensive process that delays mass adoption despite pilot production. Company press releases frame shipments as "prototype" or "samples" for customer evaluation, not full production-ready cells. Source: QuantumScape and ProLogium press language noting prototype/sample shipments and ongoing qualification steps. (https://www.quantumscape.com/quantumscape-announces-shipment-of-b1-samples-achieving-a-key-annual-goal ; https://prologium.com/prologiums-next-generation-lithium-ceramic-battery-shipments-surpass-2-4-million-units-a-new-milestone-in-the-commercialization-of-green-energy-technologies)
  - Credibility: company primary; qualification timelines are well-known in automotive supply chains.

- IP / licensing / equipment bottlenecks: production of ceramic thin films and solid electrolyte handling may require proprietary equipment and licensing; companies are securing manufacturing partnerships and supply agreements. Source: QuantumScape press releases mentioning manufacturing partners and pilot line automation initiatives. (https://www.quantumscape.com/category/press-releases/page/2)
  - Credibility: company primary and SEC filings typically disclose partner relationships.


Conclusions and recommended next steps for deeper verification

- The retrieved documents show meaningful progress: multiple firms claim pilot lines, prototype shipments, and in at least one case (ProLogium) shipments from gigafactory-class production in 2024–2026. However, many claims are company-reported and forward-looking; independent third-party validation (TV reports, peer-reviewed endurance tests, OEM qualification statements) is sparse in the retrieved subset.

- Recommended next steps (follow-up research tasks):
  1. Retrieve and read primary SEC filings, OEM supplier agreements, and independent test reports cited by companies (e.g., full TÜV test reports for ProLogium cells).
  2. Search analyst reports (BNEF, UBS, Goldman Sachs, IDTechEx) for quantified timelines, cost projections, and probability-weighted forecasts.
  3. Query OEM qualification announcements (Toyota, VW, Stellantis, Hyundai, BYD) for confirmed SSB supplier selections and qualification timelines.
  4. Conduct a targeted patent- and litigation search (USPTO, EPO, CNIPA, and DocketWatch) for notable IP disputes among major SSB players.
  5. Seek independent testing/validation of claimed metrics (energy density, cycle life, fast-charge behavior, safety tests) from labs (TV, Intertek, Fraunhofer) and academic publications.
